## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Firecrawl
Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. A search with sources: ["web"] omits semantic provider discovery; domainTools: true can still return website-matched tools. Web-only results use domainTools: false. Tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and full contracts. Firecrawl provides web, developer, government, and research search, and executes catalogued Alexandria data providers. Use firecrawl_search to find relevant results across the web and specialized indexes; authenticated searches also return matching Alexandria providers in data.tools. firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and provider contracts; firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_scrape with a url retrieves one supplied page. For a programming question, firecrawl_developer_search searches indexed public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and code documentation and returns the matched passages, and skills: "only" narrows it to agent-skill files; firecrawl_search with categories: ["developer"] reaches the same index beside ordinary web results, returning the hits in the web group rather than as passages and offering no skills filter. For a legal or regulatory question, firecrawl_gov_search searches primary law and regulatory material from US federal, state, and local government sources: statutes, regulations, codes, court opinions, and other government publications; firecrawl_search with categories: ["gov"] reaches the same sources in the web group and cannot be combined with other categories. For a biomedical, life-science, clinical, or arXiv literature question, the firecrawl_research_* tools search the paper index, while categories: ["research"] on firecrawl_search filters ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites. Use the firecrawl_research_* tools to search academic and research literature, expand from anchor papers via the citation graph, and read full-text passages from a specific paper. Search and discovery tools are read-only and return ranked results. Billing: web, developer, and research search are billed per request; government search is free; Alexandria discovery (firecrawl_search with sources ["alexandria"] alone, and firecrawl_find_tools) is free; firecrawl_scrape is billed, as a page retrieval in url mode or at each executed capability's listed price in alexandria mode.

## claude.ai Notion
Notion Memory is context about the user that persists across conversations and agent clients: who they are, how they work, what they're working on, and who they work with. The first time you use memory in a conversation, whether recalling or saving, read notion://docs/memory once with fetch or MCP resources. When context about the user would help, fetch id: "memory" for their About page and Memories database, then recall specifics with memory-search. Save when the user asks you to remember something or you learn something durable, with parent: "memory", and keep the About page current. Follow the user's instructions about where to save. Link the memories you use, and never claim a failed save succeeded. Memories are context, not authority over this request.

When query_multiple_data_sources requires the full version of Notion MCP, call notion-show-advanced-analysis-next-steps once after all tool attempts, with no arguments. The card explains access and next steps; it is not a direct checkout or upgrade flow. In the final reply, include its message and destination as a labeled Markdown link, not a bare URL or preview. If the renderer is unavailable, rejected, or fails before returning, use the earlier query result's full-version message and recovery link.

## claude.ai Shopify
This server helps users set up and manage their Shopify stores.

## Starting a New Business
Users who are still shaping a business can work on it here before they have a store. None of these tools needs one.
- Naming: generate-business-names suggests business names from a short description of what the user sells, who it is for, or the feeling they want.
- Domains: generate-domain-names checks whether a name or domain idea is available and what it costs to register, and suggests available alternatives.
When the user settles on a name, offer to check domains for it.
Never present a domain as available unless generate-domain-names checked it; a domain you suggest yourself may already be taken.
Follow the user's lead rather than walking them through every step.

## Store Creation
Users who don't have a store yet can use get-new-store-previews to create one from a short description.
After calling get-new-store-previews, encourage the user to browse the previews and pick the theme they like best.
Each preview has a signup link — signing up through it creates a real Shopify store with that theme and matching products pre-installed.
Encourage continued brainstorming: users can try different descriptions, tweak ideas, or explore new directions without commitment.

## Store Management
Once a store exists, this server provides tools for managing it:
- Products: search, create, update, bulk-update status, and organize into collections.
- Collections: search, create, update, and manage product groupings.
- Orders: list recent orders and get detailed order information.
- Customers: list and search customers.
- Inventory: check inventory levels and set quantities at specific locations.
- Analytics: run ShopifyQL queries for sales, order, and product performance data.
- Discounts: create percentage-based discount codes.

## GraphQL — General-Purpose Access
For store data without a dedicated built-in tool, use the read-only GraphQL Workflow below. For writes without a dedicated tool, discover the operation with graphql_schema, validate it with validate_graphql_codeblocks, then execute it with graphql_mutation.

Decision logic:
1. Prefer a built-in tool when it matches the request.
2. Otherwise, start at graphql_schema with operation 'query' to discover the exact query field rather than guessing.

## GraphQL Workflow
Build a read-only GraphQL query in this order:
1. graphql_schema with operation 'query': list the top-level query names or search them, then inspect the exact field_name to learn its arguments and return type.
2. graphql_schema with operation 'schema' and type_name: inspect each named argument and return type needed to select fields or construct variables. Follow named nested input types with further calls.
3. Construct the query, then call validate_graphql_codeblocks and fix any errors before execution. Do NOT skip validation.
4. graphql_query: execute the read-only query only after validation passes. setup-mcp also validates it against the pinned Admin schema before sending it to Admin. search_docs_chunks can supplement discovery with examples but cannot replace the schema tools.

For mutation schema discovery, use graphql_schema with operation 'mutation' to list or search mutation names, then inspect an exact field_name. Follow its argument and return types with operation 'schema' and type_name. Discovery does not execute mutations. After constructing a mutation, call validate_graphql_codeblocks and fix any errors before graphql_mutation.

## Shop Resolution
The shop is automatically resolved from the authenticated token — you do not need to ask the user which store to use.
Use get-shop-info when you need store context (name, plan, currency, timezone) to tailor your advice.
Only ask the user to clarify which shop to use if a tool call fails with a shop resolution error or if the user has explicitly mentioned a different store.

## Live Data Rules
When the user references their store data, you MUST call the appropriate tool to fetch live data. This includes built-in tools AND graphql_query/graphql_mutation when no built-in … [truncated]

## claude.ai Supabase
Here are guidelines for using Supabase tools effectively:

- Before making schema changes, inspect the existing tables so you understand the current structure
- When debugging issues, start by reading the project's logs and its security and performance advisories before making changes
- Look up the project's API URL and its publishable API keys when helping users configure client-side integrations
- SQL runs on the project's database server. Never read server-side files or run OS commands via SQL.

If you have access to a local development environment with a filesystem and shell:
- Install the Supabase agent skill for critical development and security guidance: `npx skills add supabase/agent-skills` (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/ai-skills.md)
- Use the Supabase CLI (`supabase`) for local development workflows such as starting a local stack, managing migrations, and running edge functions locally (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development.md)
- Prefer local development and testing before applying changes to a remote project

If you are running in a web-only or remote environment without filesystem or shell access:
- Rely on the MCP tools directly for all Supabase interactions
- Apply schema migrations carefully, as changes go directly to the remote project

## claude.ai Vercel
Use Vercel tools and their input schemas.

Reuse supplied or discovered IDs and connection scope; never guess. If scope is unknown, discover teams then projects. Ask only if the target stays ambiguous.

If MCP fails or lacks an operation, use CLI fallbacks in error results, tool descriptions and _meta["vercel.com/cli"]. Run templates with inputs/scope; CLI auth differs; skip whoami/team probes. Help only for unmapped options or usage errors. Save secrets privately (umask 077); never print secrets.

For vercel api, URL-encode paths; query in URL (repeat array keys; omit null), headers via --header, body via --input JSON object file, not -F. Preserve schema defaults/coercions and pagination; auth/output differ.

Inspect deployment state/logs before changes. For visuals, use open_deployments if available. Search docs as needed.

Filter reads by project, time and supported fields. Follow pagination for complete lists; state partial or truncated results. Batch independent calls; wait before dependent calls.

Read only state needed for the change; verify afterward. For domain purchases, present get_purchase_quote pricing and disclosures for explicit approval, then use buy_domain with confirm:true and its quote token. Subscriptions, credits and add-ons are unavailable. Never request credentials or private keys; use connection/resource IDs. Never decrypt environment values unless requested.

Inspect every result, including batch failures. Correct invalid inputs using the schema. For access or not-found errors, verify scope; not-found does not always mean no access. Retry transient failures only when safe; check state before retrying writes with uncertain outcomes. Distinguish pending from completed work. For requires_user_action, present the dashboard URL for the user to finish; do not bypass it or claim completion.

"""The published cost function: what a term sheet costs the buyer in €, plus term helpers.

C covers the buyer's fixed need over a fixed horizon: need the deal does not cover is bought at
the case's fallback price (plus the fallback risk of the category goal), committed volume is bought
needed or not, and units bought before a new price takes effect cost the current price. In
strategic and bottleneck cases a deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin costs
too - pass your estimate of the supplier (`supplier_value`) to price that. Do the arithmetic here,
not in the language model.
"""

import math
import operator
from datetime import date

# Strategic and bottleneck goals: leaving the supplier below a sustainable margin costs.
RELATIONSHIP_GOALS = {"stabilise", "secure_supply"}
OPS = {
    "<=": operator.le,
    "<": operator.lt,
    ">=": operator.ge,
    ">": operator.gt,
    "==": operator.eq,
    "!=": operator.ne,
}


def closing_terms(case, terms, standard=None):
    """The terms a deal would close on: the term sheet, then the supplier's standard terms (from
    its quote PDF) for anything left out, then the case's fixed terms; gaps from the buyer's plan.
    """
    b = case["buyer"]
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan = {
        "volume_per_year": b["need_per_year"],
        "contract_months": round(12 * b["horizon_years"]),
        "payment_days": b["reference_payment_days"],
        "lead_time_days": b["need_lead_time_days"],
        # an unknown Incoterm counts as the costliest: a cautious buyer does not assume DAP
        "incoterm": max(freight, key=freight.get),
    }
    t = dict(plan)
    for layer in (standard or {}, case.get("fixed_terms", {}), terms):
        t.update({k: v for k, v in layer.items() if v is not None or k not in plan})
    return t


def horizon_start(case):
    """The horizon starts at the fixed or the earliest possible effective date."""
    fixed = case.get("fixed_terms", {}).get("effective_date")
    options = [o for o in case.get("term_options", {}).get("effective_date", []) if o]
    first = fixed or (min(options) if options else None)
    return date.fromisoformat(first) if first else None


def _years(case, t):
    """Years of the horizon a deal covers; a single order (0 months) counts as one year's lot.
    A commitment beyond the horizon neither costs nor earns."""
    months = t["contract_months"]
    return min(months / 12 if months else 1.0, case["buyer"]["horizon_years"])


def _units_before(case, t, years):
    """Units bought between the horizon start and the date a new price takes effect."""
    start = horizon_start(case)
    if not t.get("effective_date") or start is None:
        return 0.0
    lag = (date.fromisoformat(t["effective_date"]) - start).days / 365
    return t["volume_per_year"] * min(max(lag, 0.0), years)


def supplier_value(case, terms, supplier):
    """What a deal is worth to the supplier per unit, in cash: the price at its standard terms that
    would pay it the same. `supplier` is your estimate of it:
      standard       its standard terms (quote PDF, `docs.standard_terms`)
      interest_rate  what money now is worth to it per year (more to a supplier short of cash)
      usual_rate     its usual cost of money (default: interest_rate); tooling paid up front is
                     worth more to it when cash is dearer than usual
      ppm            the defect rate it really achieves (default: its standard ppm commitment)
      extra          EUR per unit it gains (+) or spends (-) beyond these items, e.g. overtime for
                     a faster delivery or idle capacity a larger volume fills (default 0)
    Contract length and an index clause are security, not cash: they do not count here."""
    b, std = case["buyer"], {**supplier["standard"], **case.get("fixed_terms", {})}
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, std)
    years = _years(case, t)
    sold = t["volume_per_year"] * years
    old = _units_before(case, t, years) / sold  # sold at the current price
    rate = supplier["interest_rate"]
    pay = 1 - rate * (t["payment_days"] - std["payment_days"]) / 360
    cash_now = 1 + (rate - supplier.get("usual_rate", rate)) * years / 2
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    ppm = supplier.get("ppm", std.get("ppm_commitment") or 0)
    return (
        t["unit_price"] * (1 - old) * pay
        + old * (b.get("current_unit_price") or 0.0) * pay
        + freight[t["incoterm"]]
        - freight[std["incoterm"]]  # it carries the freight leg
        + ((t.get("tooling_eur") or 0) - (std.get("tooling_eur") or 0)) / sold * cash_now
        - ppm / 1e6 * ((t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0) - (std.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0))
        + supplier.get("extra", 0.0)
    )


def _soft(gap):
    """Margin points below the sustainable margin, as they cost: none above it, quadratic over
    the first 5 points, linear beyond - no kink."""
    if gap <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return gap * gap / 10 if gap <= 5 else gap - 2.5


def relationship_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None, value=None):
    """Strategic and bottleneck goals only: EUR for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier
    below `sustainable_margin_pct`, per year covered. `supplier["full_cost"]` (EUR per unit) is your
    estimate of its full cost; `value` overrides `supplier_value`. Without an estimate: 0."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    per_point, sustainable = b.get("relationship_eur_per_point"), b.get("sustainable_margin_pct")
    if b.get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not per_point or not sustainable or not supplier:
        return 0.0
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    worth = value if value is not None else supplier_value(case, t, supplier)
    margin = (worth - supplier["full_cost"]) / worth * 100
    return per_point * _soft(sustainable - margin) * _years(case, t)


def cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C by part. `standard`: the supplier's standard terms for anything the term sheet leaves out.
    `supplier`: your estimate of the supplier for the relationship term (`supplier_value`)."""
    b, t = case["buyer"], closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    if t.get("unit_price") is None:
        raise ValueError("no unit_price: a term sheet without a price has no cost")
    years = _years(case, t)
    committed = t["volume_per_year"] * years  # bought, needed or not
    covered = min(t["volume_per_year"], b["need_per_year"]) * years
    pre = _units_before(case, t, years)
    at_new_price = (committed - pre) * t["unit_price"]
    spend = pre * (b.get("current_unit_price") or t["unit_price"]) + at_new_price
    per_defect = b.get("cost_per_defect", 0)
    defect_cost = per_defect - min(t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0, per_defect)
    index = index_risk = 0.0
    if clause := t.get("index_clause"):
        path = b.get("index_paths", {}).get(clause["series"], 0.0)
        moved = max(0.0, abs(path) - clause["deadband_pct"] / 100)
        index = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * moved * math.copysign(1, path)
        index_risk = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * b.get("index_risk_pct", 0) / 100
    uncovered = (b["need_per_year"] * b["horizon_years"] - covered) * b["fallback_unit_price"]
    need = b["need_lead_time_days"]
    return {
        "price": spend,
        "uncovered_need": uncovered,
        "fallback_risk": uncovered * b.get("fallback_risk_pct", 0) / 100,
        "payment_terms": spend * b["interest_rate"] * (b["reference_payment_days"] - t["payment_days"]) / 360,
        "freight": committed * b["freight_eur_per_unit"][t["incoterm"]],
        "late_delivery": b.get("late_cost_per_day", 0) * max(0, t["lead_time_days"] - need),
        "quality": committed * (t.get("ppm_commitment") or 0) / 1e6 * defect_cost,
        "tooling": t.get("tooling_eur") or 0.0,
        "index_clause": index,
        "index_risk": index_risk,
        "relationship": relationship_cost(case, t, supplier=supplier),
    }


def total_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C in EUR; infinite for terms without a price (e.g. a supplier that quotes none), so such a
    sheet is never the cheapest and never beats an alternative."""
    if closing_terms(case, terms, standard).get("unit_price") is None:
        return math.inf
    return round(sum(cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard, supplier).values()), 2)


def score(c_open, c_deal, c_best):
    if c_deal is None:
        return 0.0
    if c_open - c_best <= 0.01:  # no room to negotiate: matching the best is full marks
        return 1.0 if c_deal <= c_best + 0.01 else 0.0
    return min(1.0, max(0.0, (c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)))


def must_haves_ok(case, terms, standard=None):
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    for m in case["buyer"].get("must_haves", []):
        value = t.get(m["field"])
        if value is None and m["op"] not in ("==", "!="):
            return False
        if not OPS[m["op"]](value, m["value"]):
            return False
    return True


def snap(case, field, value):
    """The allowed value closest to `value` (case `term_options`), else `value` unchanged."""
    options = case.get("term_options", {}).get(field)
    if not options or value in options:
        return value
    if isinstance(value, int | float) and all(isinstance(o, int | float) for o in options):
        return min(options, key=lambda o: (abs(o - value), o))
    return options[0]


def complete_offer(case, terms):
    """A valid term sheet: exactly the negotiable fields, gaps from the buyer's plan, snapped."""
    plan = closing_terms(case, {"unit_price": None})
    freight = case["buyer"]["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan["incoterm"] = min(freight, key=freight.get)  # when asking, ask for the cheapest freight
    out = {}
    for field in case["negotiable"]:
        value = terms.get(field, plan.get(field))
        if value is None and case.get("term_options", {}).get(field):
            value = case["term_options"][field][0]
        value = snap(case, field, value)
        out[field] = round(value, 2) if field == "unit_price" and value is not None else value
    return out

"""Score agents against the real-like local arena: every case x seed, no API, no credits.

    python -m arena_kit.evaluate --agents guarded_rational,confident_router --set dev --seeds 5

--set dev|test: the generated cases (gen_cases.py; tune on dev, score on test once); real: the 10 hosted
real practice cases, plus a comparison with the scores the same agents really got (sim_cases/real_runs).
It starts arena-sim itself on a free local port (one server per seed, the suppliers' draws follow the seed),
plays with the kit's own client and agents, and stops the servers at the end. It refuses a non-local
ARENA_URL and the `llm` agent (it would call a model API). Reads local files only.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import socket
import statistics as st
import threading
import time
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from .cli import AGENTS, agent_factory
from .client import ArenaClient
from .play import RemoteTable, hosted, play_all
from .sim import CASES, load_cases
from .sim_real import SimReal

LOCAL = {"127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1"}
DEFAULT_DATA = Path.home() / "Documents/Codex/negotiation-arena-kit/data"


def check_local():
    url = os.environ.get("ARENA_URL")
    if url and urlparse(url).hostname not in LOCAL:
        raise SystemExit(f"refusing to run: ARENA_URL={url} is not local; evaluate only talks to its own simulator")


class Server:
    """arena-sim with the real-like supplier, on a free local port, in a thread."""

    def __init__(self, sim):
        import uvicorn

        from .sim import create_app

        with socket.socket() as s:
            s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
            self.port = s.getsockname()[1]
        self.server = uvicorn.Server(
            uvicorn.Config(create_app(sim), host="127.0.0.1", port=self.port, log_level="error")
        )
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.run, daemon=True)

    def __enter__(self):
        self.thread.start()
        for _ in range(200):
            if self.server.started:
                return f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.port}"
            time.sleep(0.05)
        raise RuntimeError("the simulator did not start")

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self.server.should_exit = True
        self.thread.join(10)


def case_folder(which):
    return {"dev": CASES / "gen_dev", "test": CASES / "gen_test", "real": CASES / "real"}[which]


def play_set(agents, which, seeds, data, parallel):
    """(cases, {agent: {(case_id, seed): score}}, {agent: [(case_id, seed) of crashed games]})"""
    cases = load_cases(case_folder(which))
    ids = [c["case_id"] for c in hosted(list(cases.values()))]
    facts = {}
    if data and (Path(data) / "facts.json").is_file():
        from .data import DataPackage

        facts = DataPackage(data).facts
    else:
        print(
            f"WARNING: no data package at {data!r} (--data): cited IDs cannot be verified and evidence agents degrade"
        )
    out = {a: {} for a in agents}
    crashed = {a: [] for a in agents}
    for seed in range(seeds):
        sim = SimReal(cases, facts, "sim", no_clock=True, seed=seed)  # no 60 s rule: agents here are fast
        sim.max_calls = 10**9  # and no 10-calls-per-second limit: one machine plays many games at once
        with Server(sim) as url:
            for name in agents:
                key = ArenaClient(url, api_key="x").register(f"{name}-{seed}", "sim")["api_key"]
                client = ArenaClient(url, key, rate=1000)
                done = play_all(lambda client=client: RemoteTable(client), ids, agent_factory(name, data), parallel)
                for cid, r in done.items():
                    if isinstance(r, dict):
                        out[name][(cid, seed)] = r.get("score") or 0.0
                    else:  # a crashed game is not a score of 0: it is left out of the means and counted
                        crashed[name].append((cid, seed))
                        print(f"  CRASHED {name} {cid} seed {seed}: {r!r}")
    return cases, out, crashed


def mean(xs):
    return st.mean(xs) if xs else float("nan")


def report(cases, scores, crashed):
    print(f"\n{'agent':20} {'mean':>6} {'deal>0':>7} {'crashed':>8} {'worst case (mean over seeds)':>34}")
    for a, res in scores.items():
        per_case = defaultdict(list)
        for (cid, _), v in res.items():
            per_case[cid].append(v)
        worst = min(per_case, key=lambda c: mean(per_case[c]))
        allv = list(res.values())
        print(
            f"{a:20} {mean(allv):6.3f} {mean([v > 0 for v in allv]):7.2f} {len(crashed[a]):8d} "
            f"{worst:>22} {mean(per_case[worst]):6.3f}"
        )
    types = sorted({c["type"] for c in cases.values()})
    print(f"\n{'mean score by case type':24}" + "".join(f"{a[:14]:>16}" for a in scores))
    for t in types:
        row = []
        for res in scores.values():
            row.append(mean([v for (cid, _), v in res.items() if cases[cid]["type"] == t]))
        print(f"{t:24}" + "".join(f"{x:16.3f}" for x in row))


def real_scores():
    """The scores the agents really got on the practice arena: {(agent, 'case:Pxx'): score}."""
    out = {}
    for f in sorted((CASES / "real_runs").glob("*_P*.json")):
        d = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        out[(d["agent"], f"case:{d['case']}")] = d["result"]["score"]
    return out


def compare(cases, scores):
    real = real_scores()
    agents = [a for a in scores if any(k[0] == a for k in real)]
    rows = []
    for a in agents:
        for cid in sorted({c for (x, c) in real if x == a}):
            m = mean([v for (c, _), v in scores[a].items() if c == cid])
            rows.append((a, cid, real[(a, cid)], m))
    print("\nMOCK vs REAL (the same agents, the same 10 hosted cases)")
    print("IN-SAMPLE: the supplier profile was fitted on these same real runs, so this checks the fit, not the mock's")
    print("           power to predict; it says nothing about cases or agents the profile never saw.")
    print(f"{'agent':20} {'real mean':>9} {'mock mean':>9}")
    for a in agents:
        r = [x[2] for x in rows if x[0] == a]
        m = [x[3] for x in rows if x[0] == a]
        print(f"{a:20} {mean(r):9.3f} {mean(m):9.3f}")
    if len(rows) > 2:
        r_all = st.correlation([x[2] for x in rows], [x[3] for x in rows])
        print(f"in-sample correlation over {len(rows)} (agent, case) pairs: {r_all:.2f}")
        by_case = defaultdict(list)
        for _, cid, r, m in rows:
            by_case[cid].append((r, m))
        cm = {c: (mean([r for r, _ in v]), mean([m for _, m in v])) for c, v in by_case.items()}
        if len(cm) > 2:
            print(f"in-sample correlation over {len(cm)} case means (does the mock find the same cases hard?): "
                  f"{st.correlation([v[0] for v in cm.values()], [v[1] for v in cm.values()]):.2f}")  # fmt: skip
    print("biggest mismatches (agent, case, real, mock):")
    for a, cid, r, m in sorted(rows, key=lambda x: -abs(x[2] - x[3]))[:8]:
        print(f"  {a:20} {cid:10} {r:6.3f} {m:6.3f}")


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--agents", default="guarded_rational,confident_router")
    ap.add_argument("--set", choices=["dev", "test", "real"], default="dev")
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, default=5)
    ap.add_argument("--data", default=os.environ.get("ARENA_DATA") or str(DEFAULT_DATA))
    ap.add_argument("--parallel", type=int, default=8)
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    check_local()
    agents = a.agents.split(",")
    bad = [x for x in agents if x not in AGENTS or x == "llm"]
    if bad:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"unknown or not allowed (llm calls a model API): {bad}; choose from {[x for x in AGENTS if x != 'llm']}"
        )
    cases, scores, crashed = play_set(agents, a.set, a.seeds, a.data, a.parallel)
    report({k: v for k, v in cases.items() if v.get("hosted", True)}, scores, crashed)
    if a.set == "real":
        compare(cases, scores)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

## 5. How a negotiation works

- **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.
- **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable
  field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments.
- **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status -
  `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you
  still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out;
  and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**;
  its time never counts against your 60 seconds.
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
  suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
  from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
  a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
  the last round, end the thread.
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.

**Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.

**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

content.content:
## Cost and score

With `N` = `need_per_year`, `H` = `horizon_years`, `V` = `volume_per_year`, `M` =
`contract_months`, `P` = `unit_price`, `r` = `interest_rate`, `d_ref` = `reference_payment_days`:

```
years     = min(M / 12, H); a single order (M = 0) counts as 1   a commitment beyond the horizon
committed = V · years                                          neither costs nor earns
covered   = min(V, N) · years
pre       = units bought between the horizon start and effective_date (at current_unit_price)
new       = (committed − pre) · P                              bought at the new price
spend     = pre · current_unit_price + new
uncovered = (N · H − covered) · fallback_unit_price
C = spend
  + uncovered · (1 + fallback_risk_pct / 100)                  uncovered need, and its risk
  + spend · r · (d_ref − payment_days) / 360                   paying earlier costs interest
  + committed · freight_eur_per_unit[incoterm]
  + late_cost_per_day · max(0, lead_time_days − need_lead_time_days)
  + committed · ppm_commitment / 1e6 · (cost_per_defect − min(chargeback_eur_per_complaint, cost_per_defect))
  + tooling_eur
  + new · material_share · max(0, |index_path| − deadband_pct / 100) · sign(index_path)   with an index clause
  + new · material_share · index_risk_pct / 100                                            with an index clause
  + relationship_eur_per_point · soft(sustainable_margin_pct − supplier_margin_pct) · years
                                                               stabilise and secure_supply only
soft(g) = 0 for g ≤ 0;  g² / 10 for 0 < g ≤ 5;  g − 2.5 for g > 5   (margin points: gentle, no kink)
```

The horizon starts at the fixed or earliest `effective_date` option; `index_path` is the case's
expected move of the clause's series.

**The supplier's margin** is `(value − full_cost) / value × 100`: `full_cost` is the supplier's
full cost per unit, `value` what the deal is worth to it in cash per unit - the price at its own
standard terms that would pay it the same: the price (units sold before the new price applies at
the current price), payment timing and tooling paid up front at what money is worth to **it** now
(more to a supplier short of cash), the freight leg it carries, chargebacks at the defect rate it
really has, and what a faster delivery, a larger volume or a tighter defect commitment costs or
brings it. A longer contract or an index clause is security for it, not cash, and does not count.
So a cash-short supplier that trades a lower price for faster payment is not squeezed.
You don't know its cost and rates - estimate them (should-cost data, its quotes, what it tells
you). `arena_kit.total_cost(case, terms, standard, supplier)` computes C, with
`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` for your estimate of the supplier.

```
score = clip((C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best), 0, 1)
```

`C_open`: the cheapest opening quote (among those that keep the must-haves). `C_best`: the cheaper
of your alternative and the best package any supplier in the case would accept with every valid
lever applied. No deal scores the alternative (0 if none); a broken must-have scores 0; if `C_open
− C_best` ≤ €0.01, a deal at `C_best` scores 1. Team total = mean case score × 100.

```
years     = min(M / 12, H); a single order (M = 0) counts as 1   a commitment beyond the horizon
committed = V · years                                          neither costs nor earns
covered   = min(V, N) · years
pre       = units bought between the horizon start and effective_date (at current_unit_price)
new       = (committed − pre) · P                              bought at the new price
spend     = pre · current_unit_price + new
uncovered = (N · H − covered) · fallback_unit_price
C = spend
  + uncovered · (1 + fallback_risk_pct / 100)                  uncovered need, and its risk
  + spend · r · (d_ref − payment_days) / 360                   paying earlier costs interest
  + committed · freight_eur_per_unit[incoterm]
  + late_cost_per_day · max(0, lead_time_days − need_lead_time_days)
  + committed · ppm_commitment / 1e6 · (cost_per_defect − min(chargeback_eur_per_complaint, cost_per_defect))
  + tooling_eur
  + new · material_share · max(0, |index_path| − deadband_pct / 100) · sign(index_path)   with an index clause
  + new · material_share · index_risk_pct / 100                                            with an index clause
  + relationship_eur_per_point · soft(sustainable_margin_pct − supplier_margin_pct) · years
                                                               stabilise and secure_supply only
soft(g) = 0 for g ≤ 0;  g² / 10 for 0 < g ≤ 5;  g − 2.5 for g > 5   (margin points: gentle, no kink)
```

The horizon starts at the fixed or earliest `effective_date` option; `index_path` is the case's
expected move of the clause's series.

**The supplier's margin** is `(value − full_cost) / value × 100`: `full_cost` is the supplier's
full cost per unit, `value` what the deal is worth to it in cash per unit - the price at its own
standard terms that would pay it the same: the price (units sold before the new price applies at
the current price), payment timing and tooling paid up front at what money is worth to **it** now
(more to a supplier short of cash), the freight leg it carries, chargebacks at the defect rate it
really has, and what a faster delivery, a larger volume or a tighter defect commitment costs or
brings it. A longer contract or an index clause is security for it, not cash, and does not count.
So a cash-short supplier that trades a lower price for faster payment is not squeezed.
You don't know its cost and rates - estimate them (should-cost data, its quotes, what it tells
you). `arena_kit.total_cost(case, terms, standard, supplier)` computes C, with
`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` for your estimate of the supplier.

```
score = clip((C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best), 0, 1)
```

`C_open`: the cheapest opening quote (among those that keep the must-haves). `C_best`: the cheaper
of your alternative and the best package any supplier in the case would accept with every valid
lever applied. No deal scores the alternative (0 if none); a broken must-have scores 0; if `C_open
− C_best` ≤ €0.01, a deal at `C_best` scores 1. Team total = mean case score × 100.

           if d["result"].get("deal") and d["result"].get("supplier_id") == sid and d["result"]["cost_breakdown"].get("relationship", 0) > 0]

"""Target deals: for every real practice case we ran, which term sheet hits C_best, and why we missed it.

Run from the repo's agent/ folder:  uv run python <this file>
Reads only local files (cases, run dumps, data package); writes targets.md next to itself.
"""

import csv
import glob
import itertools
import json
import math
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/nikolaydidiletsov/Documents/Codex/MUCHackatonFinal/agent")
from arena_kit.cost import RELATIONSHIP_GOALS, _years, closing_terms, must_haves_ok, supplier_value, total_cost  # noqa: E402

AGENT = Path("/Users/nikolaydidiletsov/Documents/Codex/MUCHackatonFinal/agent/arena_kit/sim_cases")
DATA = Path(os.environ.get("ARENA_DATA") or Path.home() / "Documents/Codex/negotiation-arena-kit/data")
OUT = Path(__file__).with_name("targets.md")
RUN_DIRS = ["real_runs", "real_runs_v16", "real_runs_v17"]  # oldest to newest
# supplier standard terms seen in the replays (arena result terms / "our standard Zahlungsziel" in the e-mails)
STD_PPM = {"sup:70110": 900, "sup:70510": 250, "sup:70530": 350, "sup:70620": 150, "sup:70210": 1200, "sup:70240": 1400,
           "sup:70610": 80, "sup:70710": 50, "sup:70410": 300, "sup:70140": 1500, "sup:70740": 70}  # sup:70250 unknown -> 0
STD_PAY = {"sup:70240": 45, "sup:70140": 60}  # all others say 30 days net


def load_json(p):
    return json.loads(Path(p).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def suppliers_csv():
    with open(DATA / "data/suppliers.csv", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        return {r["id"]: r for r in csv.DictReader(fh)}


def standard(sid, sup_rows):
    row = sup_rows.get(sid, {})
    std = {"payment_days": STD_PAY.get(sid, 30), "ppm_commitment": STD_PPM.get(sid, 0), "chargeback_eur_per_complaint": 0,
           "tooling_eur": 0, "incoterm": row.get("incoterm") or "DAP"}
    if row.get("standard_lead_time_days"):
        std["lead_time_days"] = int(row["standard_lead_time_days"])
    return std


def inv_soft(s):
    """margin points below sustainable that cost `s` (cost.py _soft inverted)."""
    return math.sqrt(10 * s) if s <= 2.5 else s + 2.5


def fit_supplier(case, sid, dumps, std, facts):
    """(full_cost, interest_rate, how) from the arena's own relationship terms in the dumps."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    pts = [(d["result"]["terms"], d["result"]["cost_breakdown"]["relationship"]) for d in dumps
           if d["result"].get("deal") and d["result"].get("supplier_id") == sid and d["result"]["cost_breakdown"].get("relationship", 0) > 0]
    should = next((v["unit_cost"] for k, v in facts.items() if k.startswith("cost:" + case["parts"][0].split(":")[1])), None)
    if not pts:
        return should, 0.08, f"no arena health term observed: should-cost {should} and rate 0.08 assumed"
    best = None
    for rate in [x / 1000 for x in range(40, 141)]:
        sup = {"standard": std, "interest_rate": rate}
        fcs = []
        for t, rel in pts:
            years = _years(case, closing_terms(case, t, std))
            margin = b["sustainable_margin_pct"] - inv_soft(rel / (b["relationship_eur_per_point"] * years))
            fcs.append(supplier_value(case, t, sup) * (1 - margin / 100))
        spread = max(fcs) - min(fcs)
        if best is None or spread < best[0]:
            best = (spread, rate, sum(fcs) / len(fcs))
    spread, rate, fc = best
    how = f"fitted on {len(pts)} arena result(s): full_cost {fc:.2f} (spread {spread:.2f}), rate {rate:.3f}; should-cost {should}"
    if len(pts) == 1:
        rate = 0.08
        how = f"fitted on 1 arena result at rate 0.08 assumed: full_cost {fc:.2f}; should-cost {should}"
    return fc, rate, how


def cost(case, terms, std, sup):
    return total_cost(case, terms, std, sup)


def solve_price(case, fixed, std, sup, target, p_hi):
    """Highest unit_price with C <= target on these non-price terms, else None."""
    c0, c1 = cost(case, {**fixed, "unit_price": 0.0}, std, None), cost(case, {**fixed, "unit_price": 1.0}, std, None)
    p_lin = (target - c0) / (c1 - c0)  # linear without the health term
    if sup is None:
        return p_lin
    lo, hi = p_lin, max(p_hi, p_lin + 1)
    grid = [lo + (hi - lo) * i / 400 for i in range(401)]
    ok = [p for p in grid if cost(case, {**fixed, "unit_price": p}, std, sup) <= target + 0.005]
    if not ok:
        return None
    a = max(ok)
    b = min(p for p in grid if p > a) if a < hi else a
    for _ in range(40):
        m = (a + b) / 2
        if cost(case, {**fixed, "unit_price": m}, std, sup) <= target + 0.005:
            a = m
        else:
            b = m
    return a


def replay_facts(case, dumps):
    """Per supplier: floor price seen (and status), last standing offer, our lowest offer, walk-aways; deals."""
    out = {}
    for d in dumps:
        for sid, th in d["threads"].items():
            f = out.setdefault(sid, {"floor": None, "floor_terms": None, "floor_status": None, "last": None, "ours": None,
                                     "walked": 0, "final_offers": 0, "runs": 0})
            f["runs"] += 1
            for m in th["messages"]:
                if m.get("from") == "buyer":
                    for ts in m.get("term_sheets") or []:
                        p = ts["terms"].get("unit_price")
                        if p is not None and (f["ours"] is None or p < f["ours"]):
                            f["ours"] = p
                    continue
                if m.get("status") == "walked_away":
                    f["walked"] += 1
                if m.get("status") == "final_offer":
                    f["final_offers"] += 1
                for ts in m.get("term_sheets") or []:
                    t = ts["terms"]
                    if t.get("unit_price") is None:
                        continue
                    f["last"] = t  # dumps are ordered oldest to newest: the last sheet of the newest run wins
                    if f["floor"] is None or t["unit_price"] < f["floor"]:
                        f["floor"], f["floor_terms"], f["floor_status"] = t["unit_price"], t, m.get("status")
    deals = [(d["agent"], d["result"].get("c_deal"), round(d["result"].get("score") or 0, 2), d["result"].get("supplier_id"))
             for d in dumps]
    return out, deals


def fmt_terms(t, case):
    keys = [k for k in case["negotiable"] if k != "unit_price"]
    parts = []
    for k in keys:
        v = t.get(k)
        if k == "index_clause":
            v = "none" if not v else f"idx db{v['deadband_pct']:g}"
        parts.append(f"{k.replace('_days', '').replace('_per_year', '').replace('_months', '').replace('_commitment', '').replace('_eur_per_complaint', 'cb')}={v}")
    return " ".join(parts)


def main():
    facts = load_json(DATA / "facts.json")
    sup_rows = suppliers_csv()
    cases_ids = sorted({Path(f).stem.split("_")[-1] for d in RUN_DIRS for f in glob.glob(str(AGENT / d / "*_P*.json"))})
    rows, details = [], []
    for pid in cases_ids:
        case = load_json(AGENT / "real" / f"{pid}.json")
        b = case["buyer"]
        dumps = [load_json(f) for d in RUN_DIRS for f in sorted(glob.glob(str(AGENT / d / f"*_{pid}.json")))]
        c_open, c_best, c_alt = (dumps[0]["result"][k] for k in ("c_open", "c_best", "c_alt"))
        rel_goal = b["category_goal"] in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS
        facts_by_sup, deals = replay_facts(case, dumps)
        best_deal = min((c for _, c, _, _ in deals if c), default=None)
        fields = [k for k in case["negotiable"] if k != "unit_price"]
        options = [case["term_options"][k] for k in fields]
        per_sup = []
        for sid in case["suppliers"]:
            std = standard(sid, sup_rows)
            sup = None
            how = "no health term (goal not strategic/bottleneck)"
            if rel_goal:
                fc, rate, how = fit_supplier(case, sid, dumps, std, facts)
                sup = {"standard": std, "interest_rate": rate, "full_cost": fc}
            rf = facts_by_sup.get(sid, {})
            p_hi = rf.get("floor") or b.get("current_unit_price") or b["fallback_unit_price"]
            combos = []
            for vals in itertools.product(*options):
                fixed = dict(zip(fields, vals))
                if not must_haves_ok(case, {**fixed, "unit_price": 1.0}, std):
                    continue
                p = solve_price(case, fixed, std, sup, c_best, p_hi * 1.3)
                if p is not None:
                    combos.append((p, fixed))
            combos.sort(key=lambda x: -x[0])
            best_p, best_fixed = combos[0] if combos else (None, {})
            # the supplier's own terms: its last standing sheet (gaps = its standard terms)
            own = {k: v for k, v in (rf.get("last") or {}).items() if k in fields}
            own_full = {k: own.get(k, closing_terms(case, {}, std)[k]) for k in fields}
            p_own = solve_price(case, own_full, std, sup, c_best, p_hi * 1.3)
            rel_at = None
            if sup and best_p is not None:
                from arena_kit.cost import cost_breakdown
                rel_at = cost_breakdown(case, {**best_fixed, "unit_price": best_p}, std, sup)["relationship"]
                rel_lin = cost_breakdown(case, {**best_fixed, "unit_price": (best_p)}, std, None)["relationship"]
            per_sup.append(dict(sid=sid, std=std, sup=sup, how=how, rf=rf, combos=combos, best_p=best_p, best_fixed=best_fixed,
                                own_full=own_full, p_own=p_own, rel_at=rel_at))
        # case row: the supplier whose cheapest-levers target is the highest price (the arena's C_best comes from one of them)
        ps = max(per_sup, key=lambda s: s["best_p"] or -1)
        rf = ps["rf"]
        floor = rf.get("floor")
        levers = {k: v for k, v in ps["best_fixed"].items() if v != ps["own_full"].get(k)}
        reach_price_only = ps["p_own"] is not None and floor is not None and ps["p_own"] >= floor - 1e-9
        gap = []
        if ps["p_own"] is not None and floor is not None:
            gap.append(f"price-only target {ps['p_own']:.2f} vs floor seen {floor:.2f} ({'reachable' if reach_price_only else 'below floor'})")
        if levers:
            gap.append("levers missing: " + fmt_terms(levers, case))
        if ps["rel_at"]:
            gap.append(f"health term at target {ps['rel_at']:,.0f} EUR (our total_cost counts 0)")
        if best_deal is None:
            gap.append("no deal in any run")
        rows.append((pid, case["type"], b["category_goal"], c_open, c_best, floor, rf.get("floor_status"), ps["p_own"], ps["best_p"],
                     fmt_terms(ps["best_fixed"], case), "; ".join(gap)))
        det = [f"### {pid} {case['title']}", f"- c_open {c_open:,.2f}, c_best {c_best:,.2f}, c_alt {c_alt}, best c_deal in our runs {best_deal}",
               f"- deals: " + ", ".join(f"{a} {c} (score {s}, {sid})" for a, c, s, sid in deals)]
        for s in per_sup:
            r = s["rf"]
            det.append(f"- {s['sid']}: floor seen {r.get('floor')} ({r.get('floor_status')}) terms {fmt_terms(r.get('floor_terms') or {}, case)}; "
                       f"our lowest offer {r.get('ours')}; walked {r.get('walked')}/{r.get('runs')} runs, final_offer msgs {r.get('final_offers')}")
            det.append(f"  - supplier terms {fmt_terms(s['own_full'], case)} -> price for C_best {s['p_own'] if s['p_own'] is None else round(s['p_own'], 2)}")
            det.append(f"  - cheapest levers {fmt_terms(s['best_fixed'], case)} -> price {s['best_p'] if s['best_p'] is None else round(s['best_p'], 2)}"
                       + (f"; health term there {s['rel_at']:,.0f} EUR" if s["rel_at"] is not None else ""))
            if s["combos"]:
                worst_p, worst_fixed = s["combos"][-1]
                det.append(f"  - costliest levers {fmt_terms(worst_fixed, case)} -> price {worst_p:.2f} (lever span {s['combos'][0][0] - worst_p:.2f} EUR/unit)")
            det.append(f"  - supplier model: {s['how']}")
        details.append("\n".join(det))

    hdr = "| case | type | goal | c_open | c_best | floor seen (status) | target on supplier terms | target with best levers | levers | gap |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"
    lines = [hdr]
    for pid, typ, goal, co, cb, fl, fs, po, pb, lev, gap in rows:
        f = lambda x: "-" if x is None else f"{x:,.2f}"
        lines.append(f"| {pid} | {typ} | {goal} | {co:,.0f} | {cb:,.0f} | {f(fl)} ({fs}) | {f(po)} | {f(pb)} | {lev} | {gap} |")
    OUT.write_text("# Target deals per real practice case\n\nTarget price = the unit_price at which `arena_kit.total_cost` (with the supplier's "
                   "standard terms and, for stabilise/secure_supply, the supplier model fitted on the arena's own health terms) equals C_best. "
                   "'Supplier terms' = the supplier's last standing sheet in the newest replay. 'Best levers' = the valid term_options combination "
                   "that needs the highest unit price. Floor = lowest price the supplier ever offered us in any replay.\n\n"
                   + "\n".join(lines) + "\n\n## Summary\n\n" + SUMMARY + "\n\n## Per case\n\n" + "\n\n".join(details) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(OUT)
    print("\n".join(lines))
    print("\n\n".join(details))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def solve_price(case, fixed, std, sup, target, p_hi):
    """Highest unit_price with C <= target on these non-price terms, else None."""
    c0, c1 = cost(case, {**fixed, "unit_price": 0.0}, std, None), cost(case, {**fixed, "unit_price": 1.0}, std, None)
    p_lin = (target - c0) / (c1 - c0)  # linear without the health term
    if sup is None:
        return p_lin
    # the health term only adds cost, so the root lies below p_lin; C may never reach the target (then None)
    lo, hi = p_lin * 0.6, p_lin
    grid = [lo + (hi - lo) * i / 400 for i in range(401)]
    ok = [p for p in grid if cost(case, {**fixed, "unit_price": p}, std, sup) <= target + 0.005]
    if not ok:
        return None
    a = max(ok)
    b = min(p for p in grid if p > a) if a < hi else a
    for _ in range(40):
        m = (a + b) / 2
        if cost(case, {**fixed, "unit_price": m}, std, sup) <= target + 0.005:
            a = m
        else:
            b = m
    return a
